sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro jitaḥ kasmin bhīmaś ca balināṃ varaḥ indraprasthaṃ tvayā kasmin saṃgrāme nirjitaṃ purā
english: In what battle was Yudhiṣṭhira defeated, and Bhīma, the best among the strong? In what battle did you formerly conquer Indraprastha?

sanskrit: tathaiva katamaṃ yuddhaṃ yasmin kṛṣṇā jitā tvayā ekavastrā sabhāṃ nītā duṣṭakarman rajasvalā
english: And in what battle was Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) conquered by you — she who, O wicked one, was dragged into the assembly hall clad in a single garment while in her monthly period?

sanskrit: mūlam eṣāṃ mahat kṛttaṃ sārārthī candanaṃ yathā karma kārayithāḥ śūra tatra kiṃ viduro 'bravīt
english: You cut down their great root, like one seeking the heartwood of a sandalwood tree. You made them perform such deeds, O hero — what did Vidura say at that time?

sanskrit: yathāśakti manuṣyāṇāṃ śamam ālakṣayāmahe anyeṣāṃ caiva sattvānām api kīṭapipīlike
english: We observe the capacity for peace in human beings according to their strength, and also in other creatures, even down to insects and ants.

sanskrit: draupadyās taṃ parikleśaṃ na kṣantuṃ pāṇḍavo 'rhati duḥkhāya dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ prādurbhūto dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: The Pāṇḍava should not forgive that torment inflicted on Draupadī. Dhanaṃjaya has appeared for the ruin of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tvaṃ punaḥ paṇḍito bhūtvā vācaṃ vaktum ihecchasi vairāntakaraṇo jiṣṇur na naḥ śeṣaṃ kariṣyati
english: And you, having made yourself out to be wise, wish to speak such words here. Jiṣṇu, the ender of enmities, will leave none of us remaining.

sanskrit: naiṣa devān na gandharvān nāsurān na ca rākṣasān bhayād iha na yudhyeta kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: This son of Kuntī, Dhanaṃjaya, would not refrain from fighting here out of fear — not of gods, not of gandharvas, not of asuras, not of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: yaṃ yam eṣo 'bhisaṃkruddhaḥ saṃgrāme 'bhipatiṣyati vṛkṣaṃ garuḍavegena vinihatya tam eṣyati
english: Whoever he, enraged, shall charge at in battle, he will strike them down with the speed of Garuḍa striking a tree, and return.

sanskrit: tvatto viśiṣṭaṃ vīryeṇa dhanuṣy amararāṭsamam vāsudevasamaṃ yuddhe taṃ pārthaṃ ko na pūjayet
english: Who would not honor that Pārtha, who surpasses you in valor, who is equal to the king of the immortals in archery, who is equal to Vāsudeva in battle?

sanskrit: daivaṃ daivena yudhyeta mānuṣeṇa ca mānuṣam astreṇāstraṃ samāhanyāt ko 'rjunena samaḥ pumān
english: The divine should be fought with the divine, the human with the human, weapon with weapon. What man is equal to Arjuna?

sanskrit: putrād anantaraḥ śiṣya iti dharmavido viduḥ etenāpi nimittena priyo droṇasya pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Those who know dharma understand that a disciple is next after a son. For this reason too, the Pāṇḍava is dear to Droṇa.

sanskrit: yathā tvam akaror dyūtam indraprasthaṃ yathāharaḥ yathānaiṣīḥ sabhāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ tathā yudhyasva pāṇḍavam
english: As you played at dice, as you took Indraprastha, as you dragged Kṛṣṇā into the assembly hall — in that same manner, fight the Pāṇḍava now.

sanskrit: ayaṃ te mātulaḥ prājñaḥ kṣatradharmasya kovidaḥ durdyūtadevī gāndhāraḥ śakunir yudhyatām iha
english: Here is your wise maternal uncle, skilled in the dharma of the warrior, that Gāndhāran Śakuni who is the deity of crooked gambling — let him fight here.

sanskrit: nākṣān kṣipati gāṇḍīvaṃ na kṛtaṃ dvāparaṃ na ca jvalato niśitān bāṇāṃs tīkṣṇān kṣipati gāṇḍivam
english: The Gāṇḍīva does not cast dice; no Dvāpara throw is made with it. The Gāṇḍīva casts flaming, sharp, keen arrows.

sanskrit: na hi gāṇḍīvanirmuktā gārdhrapatrāḥ sutejanāḥ antareṣv avatiṣṭhanti girīṇām api dāraṇāḥ
english: For the vulture-feathered, keen-edged arrows released from the Gāṇḍīva do not pause in the spaces between — they can even split mountains.

sanskrit: antakaḥ śamano mṛtyus tathāgnir vaḍavāmukhaḥ kuryur ete kva cic cheṣaṃ na tu kruddho dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Antaka, Śamana (Yama), Death itself, and the submarine fire — these might leave some remnant somewhere. But not the enraged Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: yudhyatāṃ kāmam ācāryo nāhaṃ yotsye dhanaṃjayam matsyo hy asmābhir āyodhyo yady āgacched gavāṃ padam
english: Let the teacher fight if he wishes; I will not fight Dhanaṃjaya. The Matsya king is the one we should fight, if he comes to reclaim the cattle.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sādhu paśyati vai droṇaḥ kṛpaḥ sādhv anupaśyati karṇas tu kṣatradharmeṇa yathāvad yoddhum icchati
english: Bhīṣma said: Droṇa indeed sees rightly; Kṛpa also sees rightly. But Karṇa wishes to fight in accordance with warrior dharma, as is proper.

sanskrit: ācāryo nābhiṣaktavyaḥ puruṣeṇa vijānatā deśakālau tu saṃprekṣya yoddhavyam iti me matiḥ
english: A teacher should not be reproached by one who is wise. One should fight after considering place and time — this is my view.

sanskrit: yasya sūryasamāḥ pañca sapatnāḥ syuḥ prahāriṇaḥ katham abhyudaye teṣāṃ na pramuhyeta paṇḍitaḥ
english: When one's five enemies are equal to the sun in striking power, how would a wise man not be confounded in the face of their rising might?

sanskrit: svārthe sarve vimuhyanti ye 'pi dharmavido janāḥ tasmād rājan bravīmy eṣa vākyaṃ te yadi rocate
english: All people are confounded in their own self-interest, even those who know dharma. Therefore, O king, I tell you this — hear my word if it pleases you.

sanskrit: karṇo yad abhyavocan nas tejaḥsaṃjananāya tat ācāryaputraḥ kṣamatāṃ mahat kāryam upasthitam
english: What Karṇa said to us was meant to kindle our martial spirit. Let Aśvatthāman (the teacher's son) forgive it — a great task is at hand.

sanskrit: nāyaṃ kālo virodhasya kaunteye samupasthite kṣantavyaṃ bhavatā sarvam ācāryeṇa kṛpeṇa ca
english: This is not the time for internal discord, now that the son of Kuntī stands before us. You must forgive all of it, as must the teacher and Kṛpa.

sanskrit: bhavatāṃ hi kṛtāstratvaṃ yathāditye prabhā tathā yathā candramaso lakṣma sarvathā nāpakṛṣyate evaṃ bhavatsu brāhmaṇyaṃ brahmāstraṃ ca pratiṣṭhitam
english: Your mastery of arms is like the radiance in the sun, like the mark on the moon — it can never be taken away. Thus are both brāhmaṇic virtue and the brahma-weapon firmly established in you.

sanskrit: catvāra ekato vedāḥ kṣātram ekatra dṛśyate naitat samastam ubhayaṃ kasmiṃś cid anuśuśrumaḥ
english: The four Vedas are found in one place, and kṣatriya skill in another. We have never heard of both of these together combined in any single person.

sanskrit: anyatra bhāratācāryāt saputrād iti me matiḥ brahmāstraṃ caiva vedāś ca naitad anyatra dṛśyate
english: Except in the Bhārata teacher (Droṇa) together with his son — this is my view. The brahma-weapon and the Vedas both — this is seen nowhere else.

sanskrit: ācāryaputraḥ kṣamatāṃ nāyaṃ kālaḥ svabhedane sarve saṃhatya yudhyāmaḥ pākaśāsanim āgatam
english: Let the teacher's son forgive. This is not the time for division among ourselves. Let us all fight united against the son of Pākaśāsana (Indra) who has come.

sanskrit: balasya vyasanānīha yāny uktāni manīṣibhiḥ mukhyo bhedo hi teṣāṃ vai pāpiṣṭho viduṣāṃ mataḥ
english: Among the calamities of an army that have been enumerated by the wise, internal dissension is foremost — it is considered the most evil by men of learning.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmovāca ācārya eva kṣamatāṃ śāntir atra vidhīyatām abhiṣajyamāne hi gurau tadvṛttaṃ roṣakāritam
english: Aśvatthāman said: Let the teacher himself forgive; let peace be made here. For when one's own guru is being reproached, that conduct was driven by anger.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato duryodhano droṇaṃ kṣamayām āsa bhārata saha karṇena bhīṣmeṇa kṛpeṇa ca mahātmanā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Duryodhana begged forgiveness from Droṇa, O Bhārata, along with Karṇa, Bhīṣma, and the great-souled Kṛpa.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca yad eva prathamaṃ vākyaṃ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo 'bravīt tenaivāhaṃ prasanno vai param atra vidhīyatām
english: Droṇa said: I am indeed pleased by that very first word which Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, spoke. Let that be the course followed here.

sanskrit: yathā duryodhane 'yatte nāgaḥ spṛśati sainikān sāhasād yadi vā mohāt tathā nītir vidhīyatām
english: Just as an elephant touches soldiers when Duryodhana is careless — whether through rashness or delusion — let the policy be devised accordingly.

sanskrit: vanavāse hy anirvṛtte darśayen na dhanaṃjayaḥ dhanaṃ vālabhamāno 'tra nādya naḥ kṣantum arhati
english: As the forest exile has not yet been completed, Dhanaṃjaya should not have revealed himself here. Whether seeking wealth or not, he ought not to be forgiven by us today.

sanskrit: yathā nāyaṃ samāyujyād dhārtarāṣṭrān kathaṃ cana yathā ca na parājayyāt tathā nītir vidhīyatām
english: Let policy be devised in such a way that he cannot engage with the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra in any manner, and also so that he cannot be defeated.

sanskrit: uktaṃ duryodhanenāpi purastād vākyam īdṛśam tad anusmṛtya gāṅgeya yathāvad vaktum arhasi
english: Such a word was also spoken before by Duryodhana himself. Remembering that, O son of Gaṅgā (Bhīṣma), you should speak as is fitting.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca kalāṃśās tāta yujyante muhūrtāś ca dināni ca ardhamāsāś ca māsāś ca nakṣatrāṇi grahās tathā
english: Bhīṣma said: Dear child, the fractions of time are joined together — moments, days, fortnights, months, lunar asterisms, and planets too.

sanskrit: ṛtavaś cāpi yujyante tathā saṃvatsarā api evaṃ kālavibhāgena kālacakraṃ pravartate
english: Seasons are joined together, and years as well. Thus, by the divisions of time, the wheel of time turns.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ kālātirekeṇa jyotiṣāṃ ca vyatikramāt pañcame pañcame varṣe dvau māsāv upajāyataḥ
english: By the excess of time and the displacement of the celestial bodies, two extra months arise every fifth year.

sanskrit: teṣām abhyadhikā māsāḥ pañca dvādaśa ca kṣapāḥ trayodaśānāṃ varṣāṇām iti me vartate matiḥ
english: Of those, there are five extra months and twelve extra nights in thirteen years — such is my reckoning.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ yathāvac caritaṃ yad yad ebhiḥ pariśrutam evam etad dhruvaṃ jñātvā tato bībhatsur āgataḥ
english: All of what has been fully accomplished by them as has been heard — knowing this for certain, Bībhatsu (Arjuna) has now come.

sanskrit: sarve caiva mahātmānaḥ sarve dharmārthakovidāḥ yeṣāṃ yudhiṣṭhiro rājā kasmād dharme 'parādhnuyuḥ
english: All of them are great souls; all are skilled in dharma and artha. When Yudhiṣṭhira is their king, how could they transgress against dharma?

sanskrit: alubdhāś caiva kaunteyāḥ kṛtavantaś ca duṣkaram na cāpi kevalaṃ rājyam iccheyus te 'nupāyataḥ
english: The sons of Kuntī are without greed, and they have accomplished what is hard to accomplish. Nor would they desire the kingdom alone without the proper means.

sanskrit: tadaiva te hi vikrāntum īṣuḥ kauravanandanāḥ dharmapāśanibaddhās tu na celuḥ kṣatriyavratāt
english: Indeed, those joys of the Kuru line wanted to act with their heroic power right then, but bound by the bonds of dharma, they did not stray from their warrior's vow.

sanskrit: yac cānṛta iti khyāyed yac ca gacchet parābhavam vṛṇuyur maraṇaṃ pārthā nānṛtatvaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: That which would be called falsehood, and that which would lead to dishonor — the Pārthas would choose death rather than untruth under any circumstances.

sanskrit: prāpte tu kāle prāptavyaṃ notsṛjeyur nararṣabhāḥ api vajrabhṛtā guptaṃ tathāvīryā hi pāṇḍavāḥ
english: But when the proper time has come, those bulls among men would not abandon what is to be obtained. The Pāṇḍavas are of such valor that even what is guarded by the wielder of the thunderbolt (Indra) they would seize.

sanskrit: pratiyudhyāma samare sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam tasmād yad atra kalyāṇaṃ loke sadbhir anuṣṭhitam tat saṃvidhīyatāṃ kṣipraṃ mā no hy artho 'tigāt parān
english: Let us fight in battle against the best of all weapon-bearers. Therefore let that which is auspicious and practiced by the good in this world be quickly arranged — lest our purpose pass to our enemies.

sanskrit: na hi paśyāmi saṃgrāme kadā cid api kaurava ekāntasiddhiṃ rājendra saṃprāptaś ca dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: For I never see, O Kaurava, any certainty of absolute success in battle, O king of kings — and Dhanaṃjaya has arrived.

sanskrit: saṃpravṛtte tu saṃgrāme bhāvābhāvau jayājayau avaśyam ekaṃ spṛśato dṛṣṭam etad asaṃśayam
english: When battle is engaged, gain or loss, victory or defeat — one of these must come to pass. This has been seen without doubt.

sanskrit: tasmād yuddhāvacarikaṃ karma vā dharmasaṃhitam kriyatām āśu rājendra saṃprāpto hi dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Therefore, O king of kings, let a course of action related to battle, or one in keeping with dharma, be quickly decided upon — for Dhanaṃjaya has arrived.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca nāhaṃ rājyaṃ pradāsyāmi pāṇḍavānāṃ pitāmaha yuddhāvacārikaṃ yat tu tac chīghraṃ saṃvidhīyatām
english: Duryodhana said: I will not give the kingdom to the Pāṇḍavas, O grandfather. But let whatever pertains to battle be quickly arranged.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra yā māmakī buddhiḥ śrūyatāṃ yadi rocate kṣipraṃ balacaturbhāgaṃ gṛhya gaccha puraṃ prati tato 'paraś caturbhāgo gāḥ samādāya gacchatu
english: Bhīṣma said: If it pleases you, hear my own counsel in this matter. Quickly take one quarter of the army and go toward the city; then let another quarter take the cattle and go.

sanskrit: vayaṃ tv ardhena sainyena pratiyotsyāma pāṇḍavam matsyaṃ vā punar āyātam atha vāpi śatakratum
english: We, however, with the remaining half of the army, shall fight the Pāṇḍava, or the Matsya king if he comes again, or even Śatakratu (Indra) himself.

sanskrit: ācāryo madhyatas tiṣṭhatv aśvatthāmā tu savyataḥ kṛpaḥ śāradvato dhīmān pārśvaṃ rakṣatu dakṣiṇam
english: Let the teacher (Droṇa) stand in the center; let Aśvatthāman stand to the left; let the wise Kṛpa, son of Śaradvan, guard the right flank.

sanskrit: agrataḥ sūtaputras tu karṇas tiṣṭhatu daṃśitaḥ ahaṃ sarvasya sainyasya paścāt sthāsyāmi pālayan
english: Let Karṇa, the charioteer's son, stand fully armored at the front. I shall stand at the rear, guarding the entire army.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā vyūḍheṣv anīkeṣu kauraveyair mahārathaiḥ upāyād arjunas tūrṇaṃ rathaghoṣeṇa nādayan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: With the armies thus arrayed by the great chariot-warriors of the Kuru line, Arjuna quickly advanced, making the battlefield resound with the thunder of his chariot.

sanskrit: dadṛśus te dhvajāgraṃ vai śuśruvuś ca rathasvanam dodhūyamānasya bhṛśaṃ gāṇḍīvasya ca nisvanam
english: They saw the top of his banner and heard the sound of his chariot, and the great twanging sound of the Gāṇḍīva being vigorously drawn.

sanskrit: tatas tat sarvam ālokya droṇo vacanam abravīt mahāratham anuprāptaṃ dṛṣṭvā gāṇḍīvadhanvinam
english: Then, having observed all of this and seeing the great chariot-warrior, the bearer of the Gāṇḍīva, arrive, Droṇa spoke.

sanskrit: etad dhvajāgraṃ pārthasya dūrataḥ saṃprakāśate eṣa ghoṣaḥ sajalado roravīti ca vānaraḥ
english: There, from afar, the tip of Pārtha's banner shines; this is the roar of the cloud-like sound, and there the monkey on his standard screams.

sanskrit: eṣa tiṣṭhan rathaśreṣṭho rathe rathavarapraṇut utkarṣati dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ gāṇḍīvam aśanisvanam
english: There he stands on his chariot, the best of chariots, the one praised by the best of chariot-warriors; he draws the finest of bows, the Gāṇḍīva, which sounds like a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: imau hi bāṇau sahitau pādayor me vyavasthitau aparau cāpy atikrāntau karṇau saṃspṛśya me śarau
english: These two arrows together have come to rest at my feet; and two others have already passed beyond, the shafts grazing my ears.

sanskrit: niruṣya hi vane vāsaṃ kṛtvā karmātimānuṣam abhivādayate pārthaḥ śrotre ca paripṛcchati
english: Having completed his forest exile and accomplished superhuman deeds, Pārtha now pays his respects and inquires after my welfare — through these arrows near my ears.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca iṣupāte ca senāyā hayān saṃyaccha sārathe yāvat samīkṣe sainye 'smin kvāsau kurukulādhamaḥ
english: Arjuna said: Within arrow-range of the army, rein in the horses, O charioteer, so that I may observe in this army — where is that wretch of the Kuru lineage?

sanskrit: sarvān anyān anādṛtya dṛṣṭvā tam atimāninam tasya mūrdhni patiṣyāmi tata ete parājitāḥ
english: Disregarding all the others, once I have seen that arrogant one, I will descend upon his head — and then all these others will be defeated.

sanskrit: eṣa vyavasthito droṇo drauṇiś ca tadanantaram bhīṣmaḥ kṛpaś ca karṇaś ca maheṣvāsā vyavasthitāḥ
english: There stands Droṇa, and right after him Drauṇi (Aśvatthāman); Bhīṣma, Kṛpa, and Karṇa — all great bowmen — stand arrayed.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ nātra paśyāmi gāḥ samādāya gacchati dakṣiṇaṃ mārgam āsthāya śaṅke jīvaparāyaṇaḥ
english: I do not see the king (Duryodhana) here. He goes along with the cattle, taking the southern road — I suspect he is intent on saving his life.

sanskrit: utsṛjyaitad rathānīkaṃ gaccha yatra suyodhanaḥ tatraiva yotsye vairāṭe nāsti yuddhaṃ nirāmiṣam taṃ jitvā vinivartiṣye gāḥ samādāya vai punaḥ
english: Leaving this chariot-army, go to where Suyodhana (Duryodhana) is. O son of Virāṭa, there is no battle without a stake. Having conquered him, I shall return with the cattle.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktaḥ sa vairāṭir hayān saṃyamya yatnataḥ niyamya ca tato raśmīn yatra te kurupuṃgavāḥ acodayat tato vāhān yato duryodhanas tataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, the son of Virāṭa carefully reined in the horses and gathered the reins, then urged the steeds toward where those bulls of the Kuru line stood, in the direction where Duryodhana was.

sanskrit: utsṛjya rathavaṃśaṃ tu prayāte śvetavāhane abhiprāyaṃ viditvāsya droṇo vacanam abravīt
english: When the white-horsed one (Arjuna) had departed, leaving the chariot-army behind, Droṇa, having understood his intention, spoke.

sanskrit: naiṣo 'ntareṇa rājānaṃ bībhatsuḥ sthātum icchati tasya pārṣṇiṃ grahīṣyāmo javenābhiprayāsyataḥ
english: Bībhatsu (Arjuna) does not wish to stop without reaching the king. We shall seize him from the rear as he speeds swiftly forward.

sanskrit: na hy enam abhisaṃkruddham eko yudhyeta saṃyuge anyo devāt sahasrākṣāt kṛṣṇād vā devakīsutāt
english: For no one could fight this enraged one alone in battle, other than the thousand-eyed god (Indra) or Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī.

sanskrit: kiṃ no gāvaḥ kariṣyanti dhanaṃ vā vipulaṃ tathā duryodhanaḥ pārthajale purā naur iva majjati
english: What use to us are the cattle, or even abundant wealth? Duryodhana is already sinking in the water of Pārtha, like a boat that went under long ago.

sanskrit: tathaiva gatvā bībhatsur nāma viśrāvya cātmanaḥ śalabhair iva tāṃ senāṃ śaraiḥ śīghram avākirat
english: Going just so, Bībhatsu announced his own name, and then quickly covered that army with arrows, like locusts descending on a field.

sanskrit: kīryamāṇāḥ śaraughais tu yodhās te pārthacoditaiḥ nāpaśyan nāvṛtāṃ bhūmim antarikṣaṃ ca patribhiḥ
english: Those warriors, being covered by the showers of arrows impelled by Pārtha, saw not a single patch of uncovered earth or sky, so dense were the feathered shafts.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ nātmanino yuddhe nāpayāne 'bhavan matiḥ śīghratvam eva pārthasya pūjayanti sma cetasā
english: Their minds were fixed neither on fighting nor on fleeing. In their hearts they could only marvel at the swiftness of Pārtha.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkhaṃ pradadhmau sa dviṣatāṃ lomaharṣaṇam visphārya ca dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ dhvaje bhūtāny acodayat
english: Then he blew his conch, making the hair of his enemies stand on end, and drawing his finest bow, he roused the spirits dwelling on his banner.

sanskrit: tasya śaṅkhasya śabdena rathanemisvanena ca amānuṣāṇāṃ teṣāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ dhvajavāsinām
english: By the sound of his conch and the rumble of his chariot-wheels, and by those supernatural beings residing on his banner,

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ pucchān vidhunvānā rebhamāṇāḥ samantataḥ gāvaḥ pratinyavartanta diśam āsthāya dakṣiṇām
english: The cattle, tossing their tails upward and lowing on all sides, turned back and set out in the southern direction.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa śatrusenāṃ tarasā praṇudya; gās tā vijityātha dhanurdharāgryaḥ duryodhanāyābhimukhaṃ prayāto; bhūyo 'rjunaḥ priyam ājau cikīrṣan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having swiftly routed the enemy army and having won back those cattle, Arjuna, the foremost bearer of the bow, set out toward Duryodhana — seeking once more to do what was pleasing in battle.

sanskrit: goṣu prayātāsu javena matsyān; kirīṭinaṃ kṛtakāryaṃ ca matvā duryodhanāyābhimukhaṃ prayāntaṃ; kurupravīrāḥ sahasābhipetuḥ
english: When the cattle had swiftly departed, and thinking the diademed one (Arjuna) to have accomplished his task, the heroes of the Kuru line suddenly rushed toward him as he advanced toward Duryodhana.

sanskrit: teṣām anīkāni bahūni gāḍhaṃ; vyūḍhāni dṛṣṭvā bahuladhvajāni matsyasya putraṃ dviṣatāṃ nihantā; vairāṭim āmantrya tato 'bhyuvāca
english: Seeing those many armies closely arrayed, bristling with numerous banners, the slayer of enemies addressed the son of Virāṭa and then spoke.
